title: ScamShield policy, schema version 1
description: Contract between the controller app and the ScamShield Firefox extension. The controller writes this object as the value of policies.json -> 3rdparty -> Extensions -> <extension id>. The extension reads it read-only through browser.storage.managed, so each top-level property below becomes one managed-storage key. Any missing or invalid policy makes the extension fall back to its built-in strict baseline.

level.description: How firmly the extension reacts. off = nothing, reminder = gentle banner, warn = banner plus admin alert, delay = full-screen notice and the action is locked for a short time, block = locked until the admin's one-time PIN is entered.

domain.description: Lowercase hostname without scheme, path, port or wildcard. An entry matches that domain and all of its subdomains. Internationalized names must be written in punycode (xn--).

card.description: Reaction when card entry is detected on a site in this tier.

password.description: Reaction when a suspicious password prompt is detected on a site in this tier.

download.description: allow = downloads proceed, hold_risky = executables, installers, scripts, archives and macro Office files wait for a PIN, block = every download is cancelled.

schema_version.description: Contract version. The extension rejects versions it does not understand and uses its strict baseline instead.

admin.description: Who the user is told to call. Shown on every warning.

notifier.description: Where admin alerts and one-time PINs are sent. Without a token the topic is the only secret, and policies.json must be readable by the protected user, so that user could read the topic and then the live PINs. Strongly recommended: set up a private ntfy topic (self-hosted, or an ntfy account with the topic reserved and default access denied) and give the extension a publish-only access token here.

token.description: Optional ntfy access token (tk_...) sent as a bearer token. It must have write-only access to the topic.

severity_preset.description: Label for the tier values the controller applied. The extension only reads the explicit tiers below. Use custom after hand-editing any tier.

tiers.description: Reaction per list tier. Admin-whitelisted sites use whitelist, admin or feed blacklisted sites use blacklist, everything else uses graylist.

lists.description: Admin-maintained lists. Admin entries always override feed data. When a domain is on more than one list, the whitelist wins.

graylist.description: Optional explicit entries. Unlisted sites are graylisted anyway, so this only matters for the controller's own bookkeeping.

bank_domains.description: Financial sites the admin has verified. Used by bank_policy and for lookalike-domain checks.

bank_policy.description: approve_once = a verified bank behaves like a whitelisted site, approve_every = each bank login needs a PIN, off = banks follow the normal tier rules.

hold_all_downloads.description: When true, every download needs a PIN regardless of site or file type.

new_site_notice.description: Gentle notice on unfamiliar sites. once = first visit per domain, every_visit = each visit.

wording.description: Optional text overrides keyed by message id. Plain text only, no markup.

feeds.description: Public blacklist feeds. The feed URLs themselves are built into the extension.

delay_seconds.description: How long the 'delay' level locks the card or password fields while the user is asked to stop and call the admin.

card_fallback.description: Also treat any text field holding a Luhn-valid 13 to 19 digit number as card entry, not only fields that look like card fields. Catches unusual forms, but can rarely misfire on long order numbers.

seen_sites_reset_token.description: Any text. When this value differs from the one the extension last saw, the extension forgets which sites already showed the new-site notice. Change it (for example to a date) to reset.

verbose_logging.description: Detailed browser-console logging. Never includes typed text or page content.
